content:
As the 2026 World Cup draws to a close, Major League Soccer (MLS) will return to Apple TV tomorrow, with Apple Maps, Apple Sports, Apple Fitness+ and other platforms simultaneously rolling out a series of related features. Details are as follows.

MLS returns to Apple TV

Apple is highlighting the return of MLS today, with six matches scheduled in the coming days:

July 16 (Thursday):

  • CF Montréal vs Toronto FC (7:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • Chicago Fire vs Vancouver Whitecaps (8:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • St. Louis City SC vs Sporting Kansas City (8:30 PM Eastern Time)
  • Seattle Sounders vs Portland Timbers (10:30 PM Eastern Time)

July 17 (Friday):

  • Nashville SC vs Atlanta United FC (8:10 PM Eastern Time)
  • LA Galaxy vs Los Angeles FC (10:15 PM Eastern Time)

To celebrate the return of the regular season, Apple has announced a range of MLS-themed features across its platforms, including a new "Time to Walk" audio experience for Apple Fitness+ subscribers.

The new episode features German football legend Thomas Müller, who "reflects on the effort he put in before his career took off, and shares how to face the challenges of major life transitions with composure".

Apple Music will also launch several exclusive playlists curated by star players, including Diego Luna of Real Salt Lake, Evander Silva Ferreira of FC Cincinnati, as well as team-themed playlists featuring clubs from the East and West, such as the New York Red Bulls, New York City FC and Orlando City SC.

On Apple Maps, Apple will introduce "matchday guides produced by MLS clubs and city tours personally curated by players, helping users discover matchday restaurants, explore popular local hotspots, and gain a deeper understanding of each stadium".

Users of the Apple Sports app can stay up to date with the latest league action through live scores, standings, play-by-play text commentary, lineups and team statistics.

Finally, Apple noted:

MLS matches are available to Apple TV subscribers in more than 100 countries and regions worldwide at no additional cost, with Apple also offering exclusive content and access to all cup competitions and playoffs throughout the season.

To learn more about Apple's coverage of the MLS return, please click here.

Apple TV is available for US$12.99 per month, or through an Apple One bundle subscription. The platform offers a range of popular series and films, including The Splinter, Studio Storm, Morning Show, Slow and Steady, and Doomsday Storeroom.
